angle: FINAL CUT. The base is C's cinematic token match-cut spine (the judges' winner). It carries A's retention architecture: the frame-0 micro-freeze slam, the open loop 'It scales… until it doesn't.' paid off by 'No.', the racing-then-stalling speedup curve that hits THE WALL, the comment bait, SCALE n/6 kickers, π/e and vaddps easter eggs, the 80 ms gap before the biggest drop, and a pure-function crawl clock for the loop. It also carries B's honesty and mechanism clarity: one counter unit, 'CALCULATIONS AT ONCE', with a LIME ×N multiplier on every jump; a scalar-then-vector SIMD fire; async fetch/compute/write threads; warps in lockstep that then run in waves; an NVSwitch all-reduce; message passing through ToR/spine switches; 'work unit'/'result' packets; doubling lanes in the twist; and the camera-pull EXPAND rule. Every number follows one consistent lineage: AVX-512 16 lanes → a 16-core CPU (Ryzen 9 9950X class) → one H100 SXM (16,896 FP32 lanes) → HGX H100 (8 GPUs, 900 GB/s NVLink per GPU) → 100,000+ H100s training one AI (xAI Colossus 2024, Meta Llama 4). The planet is dated to 2020 and counted in its own explicitly relabelled unit. The twist uses the verified 10%-serial phrasing, '10% serial = max 10×'. All typography was measured with the installed fonts. Every line fits 6.9 units at an effective size of at least 65 for headlines and at least 39 for sub-lines, and every stack is laid out from measured bounding boxes.
title_card: PARALLEL COMPUTING · at every scale. There is no separate title card, so no frame is wasted. The kicker 'PARALLEL COMPUTING' and the open-loop line 'It scales… / until it doesn't.' carry the title in b01 from 2.35 to 4.30 s. The post title is 'How parallel computing works — at every scale'. For the cover/thumbnail, freeze b06 at local 3.45 s: the hall has just flashed cyan, the headline reads '100,000+' and the HUD reads '1,689,600,000+'. Overlay 'It scales… until it doesn't.' on it.
logline: One amber worker crawls through 320 tasks, then 320 workers finish them in a single step. The camera then pulls back through six scales: 16 SIMD lanes inside a CPU core, 16 cores with their own threads, an H100's 16,896 math lanes, 8 GPUs on NVLink, and 100,000+ GPUs passing messages to train one AI. Last comes a planet of volunteer home PCs that hit 1 exaflop first in 2020. Meanwhile a counter climbs to 1,689,600,000+ calculations at once. Then Amdahl's law answers 'infinite speed?' with 'No.': 10% serial work caps everything at 10×. The serial block turns back into the lone worker, and the film loops.
visual_motif:
THE TOKEN MATCH-CUT, THE LIGHT WAVE and THE AMBER THREAD.

THE TOKEN: a glowing rounded square handed from scale to scale (Powers of Ten). Each system collapses into ONE token, and the token carries a tiny glyph of what it contains: lanes, cores, pixels, GPUs, or a dot field. The next scale opens from that token as one unit of a bigger system.

THE LIGHT WAVE: every scale has one 'everything lights up at once' moment synced to a hit.

THE AMBER THREAD: amber is reserved for serial work. The lone hook worker stays amber inside the cyan wave, and in the twist the amber serial block becomes that same worker again.

Transition gesture per cut (so no two cuts feel the same):
- push-in into the worker
- the token opens into a core
- camera pull-back from one core
- card-flip (replacement, not containment) into a GPU
- camera pull-back from one GPU
- camera pull-back from one server, then a second pull out to the hall
- zoom-out to the planet (the cluster token becomes the hub dot)
- glitch-cut to black (pattern interrupt)
- serial block → token → worker

COLOR GRAMMAR (bg #05060A):
- AMBER #FFB020 = serial / one-at-a-time: worker and trail, serial block, the wall, the capped speedup, 'until it doesn't.', 'No.', THE CATCH.
- CYAN #16E0FF = parallel compute: lanes, cores, GPU pixels, GPUs, servers, devices, tokens.
- MAGENTA #FF2BD6 = data movement ONLY: memory traffic, the shared-memory bar, NVLink/NVSwitch, network, messages, work units.
- LIME #7CFF6B = results and gains: finished stacks, result packets, ×N multipliers.
- INK #F5F7FF = text, flashes, the instruction beam.
- DIM #5A6275 / DIMMER #262B38 = idle.
- No glow() wrappers anywhere. The post-process bloom does all the glow.

SHARED MODULE reel/motif.py. Every beat imports it, and every object that crosses a cut is built ONLY by these functions:

Constants:
- AC = (-0.35, 0.45); X_C = -0.35.
- STAGE x[-3.85, 3.15], y[-2.40, 3.25].
- Top text zone TTZ: y[3.35, 5.72].
- KICKER_Y = 6.04; HUD_NUM_TOP = -2.52; HUD_LABEL_Y = -4.00; STEP_TOP = -2.60.

Builders:
- kick(text, color, tracking=150): style.kicker(text, 34, color, tracking), centered (X_C, 6.04). Every kicker listed here measures ≤6.25 wide; the one exception is 'THE CATCH · AMDAHL'S LAW', which uses tracking 80 and measures 6.86.
- card(lines): each line is (text, style, color, t2c).
  - Styles: H96 = Inter Display HEAVY (Black) 96; H84 = HEAVY 84; H150 = HEAVY 150; S56 = Inter Display BOLD 56.
  - Lines of the same style share ONE scale, s = min(1, 6.9/widest line).
  - Stacking: the first line's TOP edge sits at y = 5.72. Each next line's top edge sits 0.14 below the previous line's bottom. All lines are centered on X_C.
  - Asserts: bottom ≥ 3.35; style.assert_safe passes; effective size ≥65 for H lines and ≥39 for S lines.
- Text conventions:
  - CARD_IN = FadeIn(shift=DOWN*0.2), 0.25 s, ease_out_expo.
  - CARD_OUT = FadeOut(shift=UP*0.15), 0.20 s.
  - SLAM = hard cut on, then scale 1.3→1.0 in 0.20 s, ease_out_back.
  - POP = hard cut on, then scale 1.08→1.0 in 0.20 s, ease_out_expo, with no opacity fade.
- hud_number(s, color=INK): style.mono(s, 96, BOLD), then fit_width(6.9). Its TOP edge sits at -2.52 and it is centered on X_C. It is top-aligned so commas never make it jump. Cache Text per string, rebuild only when the string changes, and do rolls in log10 space with comma formatting.
- hud_label(s, color=INK, opacity=0.70): MarkupText with letter_spacing 150, Inter BOLD 34, no auto-uppercase, centered (X_C, -4.00).
- hud_mult(s): style.mono(s, 34, LIME), centered (X_C, -4.00). On every jump it crossfades with the label over 0.12 s, holds 1.0 s, then crossfades back.
- step_readout(s, color): style.mono(s, 52, BOLD), fit_width(6.9), TOP edge at -2.60.
- unit(size, color=CYAN, fill=0.15, stroke=3): style.token(size, color, fill, stroke, corner=0.22). Every core, GPU and server uses this shape, so a unit scaled to 1.2 is exactly the token outline.
- handoff_token(kind, color=CYAN): base = style.token(1.2, color, fill_opacity 0.18, stroke_width 4, corner 0.22 → radius 0.264), centered on AC, with the glyph drawn above it. Glyph by kind:
  - plain: none.
  - core: 16 Rectangles 0.036×0.36, fill CYAN op 0.65, no stroke, at x offsets (k-7.5)*0.056 and y offset -0.19.
  - cpu: 4×4 RoundedRectangles 0.20×0.20 (corner 0.04, stroke CYAN w1.5 op 0.9, fill CYAN op 0.15) at offsets {-0.375, -0.125, 0.125, 0.375} in x and y.
  - gpu: 8×8 Squares 0.085, no stroke, fill CYAN, opacity 0.25 + 0.65*np.random.default_rng(5).random((8,8))[row][col] (row 0 = top), at offsets ((col-3.5)*0.115, (3.5-row)*0.115).
  - node: 2×4 RoundedRectangles 0.30×0.18 (corner 0.04, stroke CYAN w1.5, fill CYAN op 0.2) at offsets (±0.24, {0.345, 0.115, -0.115, -0.345}), plus a Line from offset (0, -0.45) to (0, 0.45), MAGENTA w2.5 op 0.9.
  - cluster: 7×7 Squares 0.06, fill CYAN op 0.65, at offsets ((col-3)*0.13, (3-row)*0.13).

Camera rules:
- EXPAND(world, slot, u, e) is a camera pull-back. Let k0 = 1.2/u. Draw a copy of the at-rest layout scaled by k0^(1-e) about slot, then shift it by (AC-slot)*(1-e).
  - At e=0 the hero unit at slot is exactly the incoming token at AC. The hero's stroke and fill tween from token style to its own.
  - Every other mobject's opacity goes 0→1 over e∈[0, 0.6].
- COLLAPSE(outline, contents, kind):
  - The outline Transforms into handoff_token(kind).base at scale 0.94.
  - Contents follow p → lerp(C_out, AC, e) + s*(p - C_out), with s = (1.128/max(w, h))^e, using ease_in_out_expo.
  - Contents opacity goes 1→0 over e∈[0.45, 0.80]; the glyph fades in over e∈[0.55, 1.0].
  - Then SETTLE: scale 0.94→1.00 in 0.17 s, ease_out_back.
  - The last ≥3 frames of every beat are the static exit_state.
- entry_ring(): starts at frame 1, never frame 0. A Circle at AC grows r 0.85→3.2, stroke INK w8→0, opacity 0.8→0, over 0.45 s ease_out_cubic, behind content. Used at the start of b02 through b07.
- hook_state(worker_idx): a pure function that draws the hook grid. b01 and b09 both call it.

Fonts: 'Inter Display', 'Inter' and 'JetBrains Mono' all cover × ∞ → … · ÷ ≈ (verified with fc-list). Always use the real '×'.

climbing_counter:
The HUD sits at the bottom. The number is JetBrains Mono Bold 96, top edge at -2.52. The label sits at y -4.00. The unit is ONE honest metric, 'CALCULATIONS AT ONCE' (simultaneous FP32 lanes), and it only climbs. A LIME ×N multiplier replaces the label for 1.0 s at every jump, so muted viewers see the multiplication.

Film-time timeline:
- 0.0 (b01): no HUD. An AMBER step readout shows 'STEP 032 / 320', counts to 049, freezes at 0.87, and at 1.00 hard-cuts to '320 WORKERS · 1 STEP'.
- 4.6 (b02): '1', label 'CALCULATION AT ONCE'. The scalar fire at 5.2 stays '1'. At 6.0 all 16 lanes land and the number SLAMs to '16' (×16, one AVX-512 instruction on 16 FP32 numbers).
- 11.7 (b03): '256' (×16), with the sub-line '× 16 lanes each' under '16 cores.'.
- 14.4–15.3 (b04): log-roll to '16,896' (×66; the card-flip makes it a GPU-vs-CPU ratio, not containment).
- 21.25 (b05): '135,168' (×8; 8 H100s).
- 27.6–28.32 (b06): accelerating roll, then an 80 ms freeze and silence. At 28.40 it SLAMs '1,689,600,000+' (×12,500; 100,000+ GPUs × 16,896). This is the biggest drop, at 59.8% of runtime.
- 32.0 (b07): an explicit slot-machine UNIT SWAP. The old number drops away, the label flips to CYAN 'VOLUNTEER GPUs · 2020', and a new count runs from 0 up to '350,000+' at 33.4. It is a new labelled unit, so it is not a drop, and it uses no FLOPS, no random digits and no ∞.
- 36.0 (b08): the HUD cracks and vanishes, then returns at 37.5 as a SPEEDUP meter, '1.0×'.
  - At 38.7, 39.1, 39.5 and 39.9 the GPUs double and it reads '1.8×', '3.0×', '4.7×', '6.4×'.
  - Ramp 40.3–41.9: GPUs race to 1,000,000 while the speedup climbs, turns AMBER at about 40.9 and STALLS at '9.9×' from about 41.0, its ticks falling silent. The value is floor-truncated, so it never shows 10.0 for a finite N.
  - At 41.9 'GPUs: ∞' and the HUD SLAMs '10×', with the label 'MAX SPEEDUP · 10% SERIAL', so the cap always appears with its assumption.
- 44.0–44.35 (b09): the HUD fades out. At 46.4 the step readout returns at 'STEP 010 / 320' and reaches 'STEP 032 / 320' on the final frame, matching frame 0.

beats.name: One at a time vs all at once
beats.mechanism: Serial vs parallel: one worker must visit the 320 tasks one after another (320 steps), while 320 workers each take one task and finish in a single step. That is the ideal no-overhead case, and the twist pays it off.
beats.visuals:
GRID (motif.hook_state; b09 reuses it).
- 320 cells: 20 cols (c=0..19) × 16 rows (r=0..15), each a RoundedRectangle 0.27×0.27, corner 0.05.
- Cell center: x = -0.35 + (c-9.5)*0.34, y = 0.45 + (7.5-r)*0.34. Extents x[-3.715, 3.015], y[-2.235, 3.135].
- Serpentine work order: r = idx//20; c = idx%20 on even rows and 19 - idx%20 on odd rows.
- Cell styles:
  - IDLE: fill #262B38 op 0.9, stroke DIM w1 op 0.35.
  - DONE (idx < worker_idx): fill AMBER, op 0.28 + 0.55*max(0, 1-(age-1)/6) with age = worker_idx - idx. This is a fading comet trail. Stroke AMBER w1 op 0.5.
  - WORKER: the cell at worker_idx, scaled 1.15, fill AMBER op 1.0, stroke INK w2.
  - LIT: fill CYAN, op = shimmer value, stroke CYAN w1.5 op 0.6.
- One VGroup driven by one vectorized updater. worker_idx is a pure function of the integer frame index f.

CRAWL, f0–f51: worker_idx = 32 + floor((f+1)/3). The worker is on idx 32 for f0 and f1, then hops instantly (no tween) at f2, f5, … f50, reaching idx 49 at f50. The step readout shows the zero-padded idx: 'STEP 032 / 320' … 'STEP 049 / 320'.

MICRO-FREEZE, f52–f59 (0.867–0.983 s): the worker holds idx 49 at (-0.52, 2.32). The headline jitters in x by default_rng(4).uniform(-0.03, 0.03) each frame. Everything else is frozen, and the audio goes silent.

1.000 s (f60) — THE SLAM:
- The headline snaps back to its exact x and dims to op 0.40.
- 'All at once.' SLAMs in beneath it.
- Every cell except the worker flashes (fill INK op 1, scale 1.3) at t_i = 1.00 + 0.35*d_i/d_max, where d is the distance to the worker, then settles to LIT over 0.25 s (ease_out_expo). DONE cells relight too.
- The worker STAYS AMBER: the lone serial worker inside the cyan field, planting the twist.
- Shock ring: a Circle at (-0.52, 2.32), r 0.2→6.5, stroke INK w6→0, op 1→0, over 0.5 s ease_out_cubic.
- Full-frame flash: Rectangle 9×16 INK, op 0.22→0 over 0.12 s.
- IMPACT SHAKE on the grid group only: seeded random offset, amplitude 0.06→0 over 0.20 s.

1.00–3.40 SHIMMER: LIT fill op = 0.62 + 0.25*sin(2π*t/0.9 - 1.2*(x - y)), a diagonal sheen.

2.35: the hook cards and the readout go out (the readout leaves at 2.85). The kicker and the open-loop card come in with CARD_IN.

3.40–4.30 PUSH-IN on the worker (ease_in_out_expo):
- Every cell maps p → AC + s*(p - W), with W = (-0.52, 2.32) and s running 1→4.178. Since 4.178 = 1.128/0.27, the worker lands at AC at size 1.128.
- The worker's own 1.15 factor tweens to 1.0.
- Non-worker cells fade to op 0 over 3.55–4.20.
- Over 3.70–4.30 the worker morphs into the token: fill AMBER op 1 → CYAN op 0.18, stroke INK w2 → CYAN w4, corner ratio 0.185→0.22 (AMBER→CYAN: the worker is a CPU core, and AMBER stays reserved for serial work).

4.30–4.47 SETTLE: scale 0.94→1.0 about AC, ease_out_back. Static from 4.47.

beats.name: One instruction, 16 numbers
beats.mechanism: SIMD: one AVX-512 instruction (vaddps on 512-bit zmm registers) adds 16 pairs of 32-bit floats in 16 lockstep lanes in one step: one instruction, 16 numbers.
beats.visuals:
WORLD LAYOUT:
- CORE FRAME: RoundedRectangle 6.8×5.5, corner 0.35, stroke CYAN w3, fill CYAN op 0.04, centered AC (x[-3.75, 3.05], y[-2.30, 3.20]).
- 16 LANES, i=0..15, at x_i = -0.35 + (i-7.5)*0.38 (x_0 = -3.20, x_15 = 2.50).
- BASE LINE: Line (-3.45, -1.55)→(2.75, -1.55), DIM w2.
- LANE GUIDES: Line (x_i, -1.55)→(x_i, 2.10), DIM w1.5 op 0.35.
- A BARS (π): width 0.30, corner 0.05, bottom on y = -1.55, height 0.16*a_i with a = [3,1,4,1,5,9,2,6,5,3,5,8,9,7,9,3]. Fill CYAN op 0.95, stroke INK w1 op 0.5.

- DIGITS: a_i in mono 34 CYAN at (x_i, -1.88); b_i in mono 34 INK op 0.85 at (x_i, 2.32).
- INSTRUCTION: 'vaddps zmm0, zmm1, zmm2' in mono 34 INK at (-0.35, 2.92), 6.47 wide.
- BEAM: Line (-3.45, 2.62)→(2.75, 2.62), INK w5, op 0 until fired.

- 0.00–0.45 OPEN: Transform the incoming token base into the CORE FRAME (ease_out_expo; fill 0.18→0.04, stroke w4→3). entry_ring() from frame 1.
- 0.10–0.40: kicker in. The HUD fades up with shift up 0.2: hud_number('1') and hud_label('CALCULATION AT ONCE').
- 0.15–0.55 BUILD:
  - The base line and guides Create outward from the center lanes.
  - A bars grow from height 0 (ease_out_back 0.2 s, staggered 0.012 s per lane from the center outward), and the π digits POP.
  - 0.40–0.70: B bars drop into their hanging spots from 0.6 above (op 0→1, ease_out_back 0.22 s, lane i starting at 0.40 + 0.012i), and the e digits POP.
- 0.70 SCALAR FIRE:

  - Lane 0's B bar drops onto its A bar (0.70–0.85, ease_in_cubic) and flashes LIME.
  - The HUD stays '1' and its number pulses 1.1→1.
- 1.00–1.15: lane 0's B bar lifts back to its hanging spot (ease_in_out_cubic) and returns to INK.
- 1.30 SIMD FIRE:
  - The INSTRUCTION POPs, and the full BEAM flashes (op 1 for 2 frames, then fades over 0.2 s).
  - 1.30–1.50: all 16 B bars translate down together (ease_in_cubic) until each bottom sits on its A top (y = -1.55 + 0.16a_i). The distances differ, but every bar lands on the SAME frame, 1.50.

beats.name: Home PCs, worldwide (2020)
beats.mechanism: Volunteer computing: a project server splits a problem into independent work units, sends them over the internet to idle home PCs, and collects the results. In 2020, Folding@home's volunteers became the first system to pass 1 exaFLOP.
beats.visuals:
WORLD LAYOUT:
- GLOBE: center G = AC (-0.35, 0.45), R = 2.75 (x[-3.10, 2.40], y[-2.30, 3.20]). Outline Circle R, stroke CYAN w2 op 0.4, fill CYAN op 0.03.
- 900 Fibonacci points: φ_k = asin(-1 + 2(k+0.5)/900), λ_k = 2.39996k. Tilt β = 0.35; spin λ' = λ + 0.30t.
  - X = R cosφ sinλ'; Y = R(sinφ cosβ - cosφ cosλ' sinβ); Z = sinφ sinβ + cosφ cosλ' cosβ. Screen position = G + (X, Y).
  - Each is a Dot r 0.022, color lerp(DIM, INK, Z), op 0.12 + 0.7*clip(Z, 0, 1), hidden when Z ≤ -0.05.
- DEVICES (volunteer home PCs): 300 points from default_rng(7) with |φ| ≤ 65°, each a Square 0.05 CYAN, op 0.25 + 0.75Z, hidden when Z ≤ 0.
- HUB (project server): the incoming token('cluster') kept at AC, shrunk to size 0.40, drawn in front of the globe, not spinning.

TIMELINE:
- 0.00–0.80 FORM (ease_out_expo): the hub shrinks 1.2→0.40. The globe outline and points start scaled 3.0 about AC at op 0 and settle to R, fading in over the first 50%. The data center is now one small dot of a planet. entry_ring() from frame 1.
- 0.80–2.40: devices pop (front side, random stagger, scale 0→1.3→1, ease_out_back 0.2 s).
- 1.00–4.30 WORK UNITS: every 0.10 s a job goes to a random device with Z > 0.35.
  - An ArcBetweenPoints(hub, device, angle 0.5), MAGENTA w1.5 op 0.4, with its endpoint tracking the spinning device.
  - A MAGENTA Dot (r 0.045) rides hub → device over 0.40 s.
  - The device flashes INK and a ring grows (Circle r 0.05→0.18, fading, 0.30 s).

loop_strategy:
1) Exact frame match. b09's last frame (f209) and b01's frame 0 are the same state, built by one pure function, motif.hook_state(worker_idx=32), plus the same card() and step_readout() calls. Verify with 'python reel/build.py handoff b09_loop b01_hook'; the difference image must be black apart from dust.

2) Motion through the seam. The worker hops every 3 frames on an integer frame clock. b09 lands on idx 32 on its last frame; b01 holds idx 32 on f0 and f1 and hops at f2. Concat keeps every frame and nothing is trimmed anywhere, so idx 32 is on screen for exactly 3 frames across the wrap (b09 f209, b01 f0, b01 f1), like every other step. The comet trail is a function of idx, so it matches too.

3) Text. 'One at a time.' and the amber step readout enter b09 at 2.40 with the same hard-cut POP every card uses, not an opacity fade-in that telegraphs a restart, and they are static from 2.60. On replay the text reads 'So why build 100,000 GPUs? Comment below.' → 'One at a time.' → 'All at once.'

4) Story. The amber 10% serial block becomes the amber token, which becomes the lone amber worker that stayed amber inside the cyan wave at 1.0 s. The part you cannot parallelize IS the one worker from frame 0.

5) Sound. Crawl ticks are individual constant-gain 'tick' cues (freq 3800, pan 0), one per hop: b09 at 1.8833 + 0.05k, b01 at 0.0333 + 0.05k. The 20/s cadence therefore crosses the seam with exactly one 0.05 s step. synth.py already wraps the audio tail onto the head, a crossfade well over 50 ms, and no hit sits in the last 0.3 s. ENERGY 0.5 → 0.55 means the bed barely changes at the wrap.

6) Film-time-periodic elements. DustField is periodic in FILM_SECONDS = 47.5, and the grain is temporal, so both continue across the wrap.

7) No end card, logo or fade anywhere. The silent version keeps identical picture, so the loop also holds under trending audio.

A counter in one honest unit that only climbs (1 → 16 → 256 → 16,896 → 135,168 → 1,689,600,000+), with a LIME ×N multiplier on every jump. The biggest drop lands at 28.4 s (60%), after an 80 ms freeze and silence.

risks: H100 numbers are not in the verified-facts sheet: 16,896 FP32 CUDA cores (132 SMs × 128, H100 SXM5), NVLink 4 at 900 GB/s per GPU (both directions combined), and HGX H100 = 8 GPUs. They are standard NVIDIA H100 specs; check them against the H100 datasheet before rendering. The 100,000+ H100 clusters ARE verified (xAI Colossus, 2024; Meta's Llama 4 cluster). If the checker demands sheet-only numbers, switch b04–b06 together to Blackwell (HGX B200, 1.8 TB/s per GPU), but first source a B200 FP32 lane count. Never drop the RTX 5090's 21,760 into an NVLink server (the RTX 5090 has no NVLink).

The counter counts FP32 lanes only. It ignores tensor cores, FMA counted as 2 FLOPs, and SMT, so it is deliberately conservative and pedants will comment. 1,689,600,000+ = 100,000 × 16,896; the '+' is there because the clusters are 100,000+.

The b07 unit swap ('350,000+' VOLUNTEER GPUs · 2020) rests on about 430,000 GPUs in the Folding@home project stats and NVIDIA's 'nearly 400,000 gamers' (medium confidence). The slot-machine swap, the CYAN label and the count-up from 0 are the defence against a muted 'drop' reading, but test it with muted viewers. Fallback: keep 1,689,600,000+ frozen and let the dated headline carry the planet beat.

'In 2020, home PCs hit 1 exaflop first' relies on Folding@home's estimated FLOPS (not the HPL benchmark), first passed on March 25, 2020. Never call it a supercomputer, and never imply it beats today's TOP500 (now 18.73 EF combined). The pinned reply can explain this.
16 AVX-512 lanes × 16 cores fits a Ryzen 9 9950X. Intel desktop chips (Core Ultra 9 285K, 24 cores) have no AVX-512, so expect 'my CPU has 24 cores' comments. That is fine and accurate.
The 10% serial fraction is illustrative. The Gustafson rebuttal (grow the problem) is expected in comments, which is the intent.

The loop seam depends on the keep-every-frame concat policy. If anyone trims duplicated entry frames, idx 32 shows for 2 frames instead of 3 at the wrap and every cut loses its 1-frame hold. Run build.py handoff for all 9 pairs, including b09→b01.

Any residual motion on a handoff frame breaks the match. Every beat must end with ≥3 static frames (b09 ends on a crawl hop, which is exact by construction), and every entry animation must evaluate to the entry_state at frame 0 (rings start at frame 1).

Measured widths assume the installed fonts and letter_spacing 150 (80 for the catch kicker). Re-run style.assert_safe on every Text, and assert effective sizes ≥65 for H lines and ≥39 for S lines. 'So why build / 100,000 GPUs?' (eff 67) and 'It scales… / until it doesn't.' (eff 70) are the smallest headlines.
